`run_local_command_modern_version` takes a new `is_detached_from_terminal` option, which runs the child in its own session so it inherits neither the caller's controlling terminal nor its process group. `run_background` and `ConcurrencyGroup`'s `run_process_in_background` / `run_process_to_completion` pass it through, so a service can get the same isolation for a long-running child.

Without it, a child that reaches the terminal can freeze the process that ran it. Redirecting stdio is not enough to prevent this: the `claude` CLI opens `/dev/tty` directly even with stdin on `DEVNULL` and stdout/stderr on pipes, and it reads that terminal and restores its modes while handling the SIGTERM this helper sends when a command overruns its timeout. Both are stopping operations from a process group that is not the terminal's foreground group -- the kernel answers them with SIGTTIN or SIGTTOU addressed to the whole group -- so the caller is stopped along with the child it was trying to kill. This is what wedged a workspace's system interface: it runs under supervisord inside a tmux pane, so it and everything it spawns sit in a background process group on the pane's terminal.

The option is off by default. Detaching also puts the child out of reach of any signal sent to the caller's process group -- an interactive Ctrl-C, or a supervisor configured to stop a whole group -- so this stays a deliberate choice made by long-running services rather than a change of behaviour for every caller.
